title: Juvenile angle closure management: The role of lens extraction and goniosynechialysis

indication: juvenile angle closure (diagnosis before 40 years; untreated IOP >= 24 mmHg with angle closure), 8 eyes with glaucoma and 3 glaucoma suspects, 8 of 11 eyes with infantile retinal laser ablation for retinopathy of prematurity; no prior incisional glaucoma surgery; lens extraction with goniosynechialysis, with or without IOL, concurrent pars plana vitrectomy and/or endocyclophotocoagulation; retrospective consecutive case series (Miami, USA)

notes: Per-eye rows exist (Table 1), so each operated eye is an 'individual' series; both eyes of bilateral patients are operated eyes (not fellow controls), so eyes of the same patient are correlated.

Reference kind 'preoperative_medicated': the preoperative IOP column is tabulated with the preoperative number of drops and oral CAI use; every included eye has at least one preoperative drop (C10); no washout described (the angle-closure definition refers to an untreated IOP at diagnosis, which is not tabulated).
Tonometer not stated in the article, so method 'unstated'.

Procedure contexts by concurrent procedures: lens extraction + goniosynechialysis alone = 'angle_mims'; combined with vitrectomy or with ECP = 'other'. Vitrectomy was usually done as prophylaxis against retinal detachment and ECP when the ciliary body was anteriorly rotated (Methods).
Inclusion required at least one month of postoperative follow-up; all patients had stopped glaucoma medications by the final follow-up (Table 1 C20).
